Bozhedarovka (Privolye Most Probably Jewish Agricaultural Colony Fraileben) Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Dnipropetrovsk Oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. Bozhedarovka (also called Privolye or Pryvillya) was established as a Jewish agricultural colony under the name Frayleben ('Free Life' in Yiddish), whose residents worked in farming and crafts — one of several such purpose-named Jewish colonies documented in this collection. According to a local resident named Ivan, born in 1948, only Jews lived in the village until 1941; those who failed to evacuate were executed in 1942. The colony was renamed Privillya in 1946, or, according to other sources, was incorporated into the existing village of that name. This cemetery, used until 1941, was completely demolished sometime in the 1990s, and its tombstones have never been located; another local resident, Efimovich, born in 1938, also confirmed that a Jewish cemetery once stood here.
